questions.q: If $r$ is the coefficient of correlation between x and y , then what is the correlation coefficient between $(3 x+4)$ and $(-3 y+3) ?$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \because r=\frac{\operatorname{cor}(x, y)}{\sqrt{\operatorname{var}(x) \cdot \operatorname{var}(y)}} \\ & \operatorname{cor}(3 x \times 4,-3 y+3)=\sum\left(3 x-3 x^{\prime}\right)\left(-3 y+3 y^{\prime}\right) \\ & =-9 \operatorname{cor}(x, y) \\ & \therefore r(3 x+4,-3 y+3)=\frac{-9 \operatorname{cor}(x, y)}{\sqrt{9 \operatorname{cor}(x)-\sqrt{9 \operatorname{var}(y)}}} \\ & =\frac{-9 \operatorname{cor}(x, y)}{9 \sqrt{\operatorname{var}(x)} \cdot \sqrt{\operatorname{var}(y)}}=-r\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $L$ is the line with DIRECTIONS ratios $ \lt 3,-2,6 \gt $ and passing through $(1,-1,1)$, then what are the coordinates of the points on L whose distance from $(1,-1,1)$ is 2 units?
questions.solution:
Since equation of line is
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{x-1}{3}=\frac{y+1}{-2}=\frac{z-1}{6}=\lambda \text { (let) } \\
& \Rightarrow(x, y, z)=(3 \lambda+1,-2 \lambda-1,6 \lambda+1)
\end{aligned}$
Now,
$\begin{aligned}
& \sqrt{(3 \lambda+1-1)^2+(-2 \lambda-1+1)^2+(6 \lambda+1-1)^2}=2 \\
& =\sqrt{9 \lambda^2+4 \lambda^2+36 \lambda^2}=2 \\
& \Rightarrow \sqrt{49 \lambda^2}=2 \Rightarrow \pm 7 \lambda=2 \Rightarrow \lambda= \pm \frac{2}{7}
\end{aligned}$
So, $(x, y, z)=\left(\frac{13}{7}, \frac{11}{7}, \frac{19}{7}\right)$ or $\left(\frac{1}{7}, \frac{-3}{7}, \frac{-5}{7}\right)$

questions.q: If $\tan (\pi \cos \theta)=\cot (\pi \sin \theta), 0 \lt \theta \lt \frac{\pi}{2}$; then what is the value of $8 \sin ^2\left(\theta+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)$
questions.solution: $\begin{array}{ll}\text { Given, } & \tan (\pi \cos \theta)=\cot (\pi \sin \theta) \\ \text { Let } & \tan (\pi \cos \theta)=\cot (\pi \sin \theta)=\mathrm{k} \\ \Rightarrow & \pi \cos \theta=\tan ^{-1} \mathrm{k}, \pi \sin \theta=\cot ^{-1} \mathrm{k} \\ \text { Since, } & \pi \cos \theta+\pi \sin \theta=\frac{\pi}{2} \\ \Rightarrow & \cos \theta+\sin \theta=\frac{1}{2} \\ \Rightarrow & \sin \left(\theta+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{2}} \\ \Rightarrow & 8 \sin ^2\left(\theta+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=1\end{array}$

questions.q: If $\tan \alpha=\frac{1}{7}, \sin \beta=\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} ; 0 \lt \alpha, \beta \lt \frac{\pi}{2}$ then what is the value of $\cos (\alpha+2 \beta)$ ?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Since, } \cos (\alpha+2 \beta) \\ &=\cos \alpha \cos 2 \beta-\sin \alpha \sin 2 \beta \\ &=\cos \alpha\left(1-2 \sin ^2 \beta\right)-\sin \alpha(2 \sin \beta \cos \beta) \\ &=\frac{7}{\sqrt{50}}\left(1-2 \times \frac{1}{10}\right)-\left(2 \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} \times \frac{3}{\sqrt{10}}\right) \frac{1}{\sqrt{50}} \\ &=\frac{7}{\sqrt{50}} \times \frac{8}{10}-\frac{6}{10 \sqrt{50}}=\frac{50}{10 \sqrt{50}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})^2+(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b})^2=144$ and $|\vec{b}|=4$, then what is the value of $|\vec{a}|$ ?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Given, }(\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}})^2+(\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}})^2=144 \\ & \Rightarrow|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}|^2|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{~b}}|^2 \rightarrow \sin ^2 \theta+|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}|^2|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{~b}}|^2 \cos ^2 \theta=144 \\ & \Rightarrow|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}|^2|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{~b}}|^2=144 \\ & |\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}|^2 \times 16=144 \Rightarrow|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}|=3\end{aligned}$
